issue.title: enabling doctest-modules causes fixture to not be found

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: indicates a problem that was introduced in a release which was working previously

issue.body:
With pytest dev (starting at: 46478fad53774fad76d829f51679824d0131a0b3) the following example passes with a default pytest run but errors if `--doctest-modules` is enabled.

```python
import pytest

@pytest.fixture
def foo_fixture():
    return 1

def test_foo(foo_fixture):
    assert foo_fixture
```

The error is:
```
____________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ERROR at setup of test_foo _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________
file /projects/251117_pytest_dev/foo/test_foo.py, line 10
  def test_foo(foo_fixture):
E       fixture 'foo_fixture' not found
>       available fixtures: _syrupy_apply_ide_patches, cache, capfd, capfdbinary, caplog, capsys, capsysbinary, capteesys, doctest_namespace, monkeypatch, pytestconfig, record_property, record_testsuite_property, record_xml_attribute, recwarn, snapshot, subtests, tmp_path, tmp_path_factory, tmpdir, tmpdir_factory
>       use 'pytest --fixtures [testpath]' for help on them.

/projects/251117_pytest_dev/foo/test_foo.py:10
```

The prior commit (543b11f2534bb0edc85b86767ed239da9c5bd140) passes in with `--doctest-modules`.

comments.body: Thanks for the report, and thanks for testing against pytest main! We will look into it before the release.

I took a quick look, I didn't confirm the below completely due to lack of time but I think it's right. @RonnyPfannschmidt this is a fun one.

With `--doctest-modules`, we collect the path e.g. `test_foo.py` twice -- once as a `DoctestModule` and once as a `Module`. Both `DoctestModule` and `Module` call `parsefactories` on the file to collect the fixtures, with `DoctestModule` first. Before 46478fad53774fad76d829f51679824d0131a0b3, the fixtures were registered with the visibility being the textual nodeid, which happens to be the same for both the `DoctestModule` and the `Module` collectors, so the fixture was visible to the `Module` and everything was fine. But after 46478fad53774fad76d829f51679824d0131a0b3, the fixture is registered with the visibility being the actual `DoctestModule` instance, therefore no longer visible to the `Module`. When the `Module` runs `parsefactories` it is ignored due to `if holderobj in self._holderobjseen: return` check.

So this is not really a problem with 46478fad53774fad76d829f51679824d0131a0b3, but more of a conceptual issue uncovered by it.

I will think on solutions later.

Ill experiment with those 

Holdrrs are now in multiple places 

Doctestmpdules are tricky

Perhaps 46478fad53774fad76d829f51679824d0131a0b3 allows us to remove the `_holderobjseen` check? That would be a nice simplification. It would make `parsefactories()` no longer idempotent, but that's not a problem for pytest core at least.

I need to check why `_holderobjseen` was needed in the first place. If it was only needed a workaround for the `DoctestModule`/`Module` problem, then that's no longer a problem; with `Node`-based visibility we can let both `DoctestModule` and `Module` register the fixtures, and they won't interfere with each other. Perhaps higher-scope (package/session) fixtures could be a problem, in that they would be registered and executed twice? But that won't happen if they're registered in conftest rather than some module file.
We may need to prepare for regression in the form of additional setup/teardown

> We may need to prepare for regression in the form of additional setup/teardown

Yes. I think it will be fine, but let's mark it as a breaking change. Even though it's a breaking change it's going to be in pytest 9.1, as it's too soon for pytest 10 and I don't think we want to revert the nodeid improvements.
For consistency we might want to consider pushing a number of deprecation into 11 to be good about semver
Thanks! This fixed the issue we were seeing in our CI running with pytest-dev.
